newsitem.title: UK: Irish bonds, UK gilts in fast track in week-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds, UK gilts in fast track in week-Salomon.

text.p: Irish bonds and gilts were the best performers in a week of moderate gains for government bond markets, according to the latest data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
Irish bonds rose 0.51 percent in punts, while gilts gained 0.46 in pounds in the week to July 17.
The Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index (WGBI) of 17 markets rose 0.21 percent in local currency terms.
The strength of sterling in recent months has had a knock-on effect on Irish punts, and strong currencies aided those bond markets in the latest week.

In G3 (Group of Three) currency markets, the firm dollar helped Treasuries to gain 0.39 percent. Dollar bloc markets Canada and Australia rose 0.28 percent and 0.13 percent in local currencies, respectively.
Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) rose 0.10 percent in yen. Bunds remained resilient to a weak mark, showing no change over the week in marks.
French and Italian bonds did slightly better than Bunds, both markets making gains of 0.06 in local currency terms.
But the strong dollar led to losses for almost every market in dollar terms. JGBs and Bunds were among the worst performers, losing 2.48 percent and 2.28 percent in dollars respectively.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
